title: Ephemeral buffer slices and gradual-shedding orchestrator for capacity-safe upgrades
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: During LTS and minor runtime rollouts we see short-lived capacity spikes and tenant impacted tail-latency as nodes drain. Existing strategies (hard drain windows + static reservation) either waste capacity or cause service surges. This ticket proposes an orchestrator that creates ephemeral buffer slices (small, time-boxed reserved capacity) and coordinates gradual shedding of pods across GPU pools to absorb transient demand without violating SLOs.
background: We currently use a combination of drain-based eviction and autoscaler handshakes. Several incidents in the past 12 months show that rapid eviction combined with bursty request patterns causes tenant request requeueing and cascade latency spikes. Our Dedicated customers expect predictable throughput during upgrades. Goal: reduce customer-visible surge events and provide deterministic upgrade pacing with minimal extra committed capacity.
proposal:
- Introduce ephemeral buffer slices per pool: small fractional allocations (1-5% of pool) that are created only for the duration of an upgrade wave.
- Slices are timeboxed and can be reclaimed early if unused.
- Orchestrator coordinates with autoscaler: announces planned slice size and drain window; autoscaler temporarily lowers scale-to-zero thresholds for buffered workloads to avoid over-reacting; scheduler packs low-priority non-tenant workloads into slices.
- Hedging rules: run a short predictive workload forecast (60s horizon) using recent interarrival and KV cache hit patterns to guard against cold-start penalties.
- Bidirectional shedding: allow minimal admit-back flow if observed load drops below forecast to reclaim slices without eviction.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag and simulation in staging for three pools (us-west-2-g1, us-east-1-g2, eu-central-1-g1)
Phase 1: Enable ephemeral slices at 1% pool size with no automatic reclamation; run controlled drain waves on low-traffic weekdays
Phase 2: Increase to 2.5% with predictive hedging enabled; integrate with autoscaler handshake and graceful admit-back flow
Phase 3: Full rollout with dynamic sizing algorithm and safety gates (error budget, tenant-latency thresholds)
Rollback: feature-flag off + immediate reclaim; if SLOs degrade revert autoscaler handshake changes
acceptance_criteria: No more than 10% increase in effective committed capacity during upgrades compared to baseline
<5% customer-request requeues attributable to upgrades in canaries
Observed 95th latency tail reduction vs baseline during drain waves in staging
Automated test harness simulates burst patterns and validates admit/reclaim logic
Documentation and runbook updated and linked in ticket
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-allocation of slices leads to increased monthly cost. Mitigation: cap slices and timebox; telemetry to track slice utilization and a spending alarm.
Risk: Autoscaler churn from temporary reservations. Mitigation: handshake protocol extension with rate-limited signals and agreed TTLs.

Risk: Unexpected tenant behavior (spiky inference patterns) invalidates forecast. Mitigation: conservative initial sizing and canary on low-impact pools; realtime rollback triggers based on latency SLO breaches.
implementation_notes: Orchestrator will be a separate controller in the upgrade-operator binary; expose CRD EphemeralSlice (flow controlled by feature flag)
Autoscaler changes: add ReserveSlices API to announce ephemeral capacity, with TTL and utilization reporting
Scheduler hints: introduce sliceAffinity label to co-locate buffered workloads; use bin-packing for non-tenant batch jobs
Metric plumbing: new metrics ep_slice_utilization, ep_slice_reclaimed_count, ep_slice_admit_back_rate
Add e2e scenario in chaos-runner to simulate sudden 3x burst during drain
